texts.li: [vow] {DEAD}, an old pilgrim of {FACTION}, has vowed to walk to the shrine at {PLACE} one last time before {X_pronoun} dies. {FACTION} have sent word: the roads aren't what they were, and they would be grateful if the colony would see {DEAD} there safely.\n\n{DEAD} will come to the colony first, and wait for whoever goes.

[home] {DEAD} of {FACTION} has been on the pilgrim roads for most of {X_possessive} life and wants to die at home, at {PLACE}. {FACTION} ask the colony to walk with {X_objective} the last of the way, since they've heard the colony's people can handle themselves on the road.

[their:friend] {FACTION} have a favour to ask, and they've asked for {FRIEND_nameDef} by name: an old pilgrim, {DEAD}, needs to get to {PLACE} safely, and {FACTION} trust the colony with {X_objective}.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will find someone else to walk with {DEAD}.

terms.li: What they ask: when {DEAD} comes to the colony, send a caravan with at least one of the colony's people to {PLACE} (about {TALE} away); {DEAD} walks with it. Within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing.\n\nWhen {DEAD} reaches {PLACE}, {FACTION} pay {COUNT} silver into the caravan's packs, and remember who walked with {DEAD}.

accepted.li: The colony will see {DEAD} to {PLACE}. {DEAD} will come to the colony first.

ready.li: {DEAD} has come to the colony and is waiting by the fire with a staff and a small bag. Send a caravan with at least one of the colony's people to {PLACE} within {DAYS}, and {DEAD} will go with it.

reminder.li: {DEAD} is still waiting for the road to {PLACE}. There's {DAYS} left.

done.li: [arrived,vow] {DEAD} reached the shrine at {PLACE}, knelt, and stayed kneeling a long time. {FACTION} paid the caravan {ITEM} silver, and {A_nameDef}'s name will be said at {PLACE} with {DEAD}'s for a while.

[arrived,home] {DEAD} is home at {PLACE}, in {X_possessive} own chair by {X_possessive} own fire, and talked the whole last mile. {FACTION} paid the caravan {ITEM} silver, and won't forget who walked with {DEAD}.
[arrived] {DEAD} reached {PLACE} safely with the colony's caravan. {FACTION} paid {ITEM} silver and thanked {A_nameDef} in front of half the town.

fail.li: [alone] Nobody from the colony set out for {PLACE}, and {DEAD} has gone on alone with {X_possessive} staff. {FACTION} noticed.
[turned] The colony's caravan turned back before {PLACE}, and {DEAD} walked the rest of the way alone. {X_pronoun} got there. {FACTION} won't say it was thanks to the colony.
[late] The caravan took so long that {DEAD} went ahead without it. {FACTION} are not pleased.
[harmed] Something happened to {DEAD} in the colony's care. {FACTION} will want to know what.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} want nothing more to do with the colony, and {DEAD} has gone with someone else.
The town of {PLACE} is gone, and {DEAD} has nowhere left to go to.

texts.li: [death] {FACTION} have word that must reach {DEAD} at {PLACE}, a town of {ENEMY} far beyond their own riders' roads: a sister of {DEAD}'s has died, and the family wants {DEAD} to hear it from someone, not from rumour.\n\nThey ask whether the colony's next caravan might carry it.

[betrothal] {FACTION} have a betrothal to announce to {DEAD} at {PLACE}, among {ENEMY}: a son of theirs to a daughter of {DEAD}'s house, arranged by letter years ago. Someone has to carry the word and the token, and {FACTION}'s riders don't go that far.

[warning] {FACTION} have heard something on the roads that {DEAD} at {PLACE}, among {ENEMY}, needs to know before the season turns: a warning about raiders, or the river, or a debt coming due. They won't say which. They ask the colony to carry it, sealed.

[peace] {FACTION} and {ENEMY} have been cool with each other for years. {FACTION} want to send {DEAD} at {PLACE} an offer to talk, but a rider of their own might not be received. A messenger from a neighbour would be.

li.label: Carry the word to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The colony will carry {FACTION}'s word to {PLACE}.

terms.li: What they ask: any caravan with at least one of the colony's people at {PLACE} (about {TALE} away) within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing, to give the word to {DEAD}.\n\nThe town that receives it pays the messengers {COUNT} silver, as is the custom, and both peoples will remember who carried it.

accepted.li: The colony will carry {FACTION}'s word to {DEAD} at {PLACE}. Send a caravan there within {DAYS}.
[warning] The colony has {FACTION}'s sealed warning for {DEAD} at {PLACE}. A caravan must get it there within {DAYS}.

reminder.li: {FACTION}'s word still hasn't reached {PLACE}. There's {DAYS} left.

done.li: [delivered,death] The colony's caravan brought the news to {DEAD} at {PLACE}. {DEAD} took it quietly, thanked the messengers, and paid them {ITEM} silver, as is the custom for bringing hard news gently.
[delivered,betrothal] The betrothal token reached {DEAD} at {PLACE}, and there was a great deal of crying and then a great deal of drinking. The messengers came away with {ITEM} silver and headaches.
[delivered,warning] The sealed warning reached {DEAD} at {PLACE}. {DEAD} read it twice, went pale, then paid the messengers {ITEM} silver and sent them off with thanks.
[delivered,peace] {DEAD} at {PLACE} read {FACTION}'s offer twice, then wrote an answer on the back of it. The colony's caravan carries the answer, {ITEM} silver, and the thanks of both peoples.

fail.li: [late] {FACTION}'s word never reached {PLACE}, or reached it by someone else's mouth first. {FACTION} are disappointed in the colony.
[late,death] {DEAD} heard of the death at {PLACE} from a stranger in a tavern. {FACTION} had asked the colony to spare {DEAD} that.

cancelled.li: The word for {PLACE} can't be carried any more: the town, or the peace with its people, is gone.

texts.li: [child] A rider from {PLACE} came to the gate white-faced: {DEAD}, a child of {FACTION}, wandered off from a family picnic yesterday and hasn't come back. Their tracks lead onto the colony's land.\n\n{FACTION} are searching the hills to the south. They beg the colony to search its own.

[youth] A rider from {PLACE} is at the gate: {DEAD}, a youngster of {FACTION}, went after a strayed goat two days ago and never came home. The goat came home. The tracks go onto the colony's land.\n\n{FACTION} beg the colony to look.
[their:friend] {FACTION}'s rider asked for {FRIEND_nameDef} by name: {DEAD}, one of their children, is lost somewhere on the colony's land, and {FACTION} trust no one more to find {X_objective}.

li.label: The colony can't spare anyone
li.outcome: The rider goes back to the search without the colony.

terms.li: What they ask: find {DEAD} somewhere on the colony's land within {DAYS}. Anyone of the colony who comes within a few steps of {X_objective} will find {X_objective}; then {DEAD} will follow them back, and {FACTION} will come for {X_objective}.\n\n{FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver, and never forget who found their child.

accepted.li: The colony is searching for {DEAD}. Someone has to come within a few steps of {X_objective} within {DAYS}.

ready.li: {A_nameDef} found {DEAD} curled up under a bush, cold and frightened but unhurt. {DEAD} is coming back to the colony, holding {A_nameDef}'s hand, and {FACTION} will be here for {X_objective} within {DAYS}.

[youth] {A_nameDef} found {DEAD} sitting on a rock, pretending not to have been crying. {DEAD} is coming back to the colony with {A_objective}, and {FACTION} will come for {X_objective} within {DAYS}.

reminder.li: {DEAD} is still out there somewhere. It will be dark in {DAYS}.

done.li: [found] {DEAD}'s mother came running the last few yards and didn't let go of {X_objective} for a long time. {FACTION} left {ITEM} silver at the gate, and the whole of {PLACE} knows that {A_nameDef} found their child.

[found,youth] {DEAD}'s family came for {X_objective}, scolded {X_objective} the whole way back to the gate, and hugged {X_objective} the whole time. {FACTION} left {ITEM} silver and their thanks, and asked {A_nameDef}'s name twice so they'd get it right.

fail.li: [searchers] {FACTION}'s own searchers found {DEAD} in the end, tired and hungry, on the far side of the colony's land. They're glad. They're not glad about the colony.
[harmed] {DEAD} didn't make it home. {FACTION} will grieve, and they will remember that it happened on the colony's land.

cancelled.li: {FACTION} want nothing more to do with the colony, and have taken over the search themselves.

texts.li: [sickles] {FACTION} have the best crop in years standing in the fields at {PLACE}, and not enough hands to bring it in before the rain. They ask whether the colony could send some of its people with sickles for a day or two.\n\nThey'll pay in grain, and in silver, and with a seat at the harvest supper.

[machines] {FACTION}'s harvester has broken down at {PLACE} with half the fields still standing and rain coming. They need hands, the old-fashioned way, for a day or two, and they're asking the colony.
[their:friend] {FACTION} need hands to bring in the harvest at {PLACE}, and they've written that they hope {FRIEND_nameDef} will be among them: their children ask after {FRIEND_objective}.

li.label: Send hands to {PLACE}
li.outcome: The colony will send people for the harvest.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: {FACTION} will have to manage with what hands they have.

terms.li: What they ask: at least two of the colony's people who can work the fields at {PLACE} by caravan (about {TALE} away) within {DAYS}, staying about a day and a half while the harvest comes in. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there.\n\nThey'll go home with a share of the harvest and about {COUNT} silver, and {FACTION} will remember who came. Half the time, half the share.

accepted.li: The colony will send hands to {PLACE}. Form a caravan of at least two who can work the fields, and send it there within {DAYS}.

ready.li: The colony's people have reached {PLACE} and gone straight out to the fields. Keep the caravan there for {DAYS} while the harvest comes in.

reminder.li: The harvest at {PLACE} is waiting, and the colony's hands haven't come. There's {DAYS} left.

done.li: [harvested] The last sheaf is in at {PLACE}, and the colony's people sat at the head of the harvest supper. They're coming home with a share of the grain, a purse of silver, and blisters.
[partial] The colony's people helped with part of the harvest at {PLACE} before they had to go. {FACTION} sent them home with a smaller share and honest thanks.

fail.li: [missed] Nobody from the colony came to {PLACE}, and the rain came first. {FACTION} lost part of their best crop in years, and they know who said they'd come.

cancelled.li: The harvest at {PLACE} no longer needs the colony: the town, or the friendship, is gone.
